claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
A 50–200 nm Al2O3 layer can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by ALD at 250–300 °C.
Post-deposition annealing below 500 °C will form or stabilize a stable alumina phase.
Post-deposition annealing below 500 °C will improve adhesion of the alumina coating to HfNbTaTiZr.
ALD will produce a conformal and continuous ultrathin Al2O3 barrier on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating and sub-500 °C anneal will minimally disrupt the underlying alloy microstructure.
The ALD-grown Al2O3 layer will limit oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C in air.
Improved coating adhesion and alumina phase stability will prevent delamination or phase degradation during high-temperature exposure.
Preventing oxygen ingress and coating failure will preserve the mechanical properties of the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
The coated alloy will exhibit lower oxygen uptake than an uncoated control after exposure at 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
The coated alloy will show minimal surface degradation after exposure at 1000 °C in air for up to 100 hours.
The coated alloy will retain the untreated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility.
The coated alloy will retain the untreated alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr oxidizes rapidly in air at high temperature.
Oxygen-induced degradation of untreated HfNbTaTiZr compromises its mechanical performance.
The proposed coating is expected to remain effective for approximately 100 hours at 1000 °C in air.
The proposed protection is expected to remain effective under tensile strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
